brief: Goldman's global macro view expects growth to hold roughly its 2026 pace into 2027 but flags downside risk from higher energy prices, higher bond yields and slower AI investment growth, and expects fewer rate hikes than priced across major developed-market central banks as AI-related labor effects become more visible and inflation declines. The GOAL Kickstart asset allocation stays modestly pro-risk (overweight equities, underweight credit, overweight cash), arguing AI, Middle East and mid-term-election risk could keep near-term volatility elevated, but earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations should help equities into year-end. Single-name calls: Apple is expected to post in-line F4Q26 results, with iPhone revenue up 15% yoy on iPhone 18 Pro/Max price increases and the Duo launch offsetting volume declines, services revenue up 10% yoy, and 47.8% gross margin. Allianz's 3Q26 operating profit is forecast about 1% below consensus on weaker P&C and asset management. DSV keeps its Buy rating and DKK2,300 target as quarterly EBIT is expected to reach DKK7-8bn in 2027. Gjensidige is downgraded to Neutral on normalising pricing, with FY27-30 EPS cut 2.4%. Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield's Buy rating is maintained despite a 2% price-target cut to €121, and the European M&A basket is refreshed with nine new additions.
